items.title: RED repro proves runSingleAllowlistedCommand ignores validate.commands[].timeoutMs
items.context: Extend packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts (already covers resolveCommandTimeoutMs and the lattice validate path in depth, per its own docstring, but never touches runSingleAllowlistedCommand) with a case that writes a temp lattice.config.json to a tmpdir project root with a validate.commands[] entry pinning a Node command plus a small timeoutMs override, then calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand with that exact command string and NO options.timeoutMs. Assert the configured override is honored (timedOut=true at the small budget) instead of the hardcoded 270s default. Must fail on current main because validation-executor.ts:595 ignores the config.
items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js` on current main prints `FAIL: hung command was killed by the per-command timer (timedOut=true)` (or similar assertion text) and exits 1 for the new section-6 case, because the ~1.5s command completes normally under the hardcoded 270s default instead of being killed by the configured 700ms override.

happy.desc: npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0 — TypeScript compiles cleanly with the new case added to validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts.

Section 6 (6a/6b) exists in validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts: 6a calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand directly with a configured 700ms override and no options.timeoutMs, asserting timedOut===false (documenting the primitive's permanent direct-call default behavior); 6b dynamically imports checklist.js's resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs, resolves the same configured override, and calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand with it, asserting timedOut===true and code===124 (proving the config override reaches the spawn through the real fixed call path).

Section 6b's genuine red-to-green history is formally recorded: red_evidence.json binds a live-reproduced pre-fix failure (baseline head ce9f57f, runSingleAllowlistedCommand ignoring the config, timedOut=false) to this story's acceptance target; the smoke's current passing run at section 6b is the recorded green counterpart of that same red state, independently confirmed by two stash-based reproductions during REVIEW (the CHK-001-correction implementer and lattice-review-concept).

edge.desc: The commanded process runtime (~1.5s) is strictly above the configured timeoutMs (~700ms) but far below 270_000ms, so the test completes fast in BOTH the red state (command finishes in ~1.5s, well under 270s default) and the future green state (killed at ~700ms). No test path ever waits anywhere near 270 seconds.
The test is hermetic: it writes lattice.config.json to a fresh os.tmpdir()-based projectRoot; no real project config or git-status side effects leak in or out.

Sections 1-5 (pre-existing resolveCommandTimeoutMs/lattice-validate-path coverage) and section 6a (the permanent direct-call characterization) all currently pass together in the same run as section 6b - the fix does not regress the pre-existing coverage this smoke already had before this story.

The lattice.config.json written to the tmpdir is syntactically valid JSON and structurally correct for configuredValidationCommands to parse (object-form entry with command, args, and timeoutMs fields) — the config is real, not malformed; the bug is that runSingleAllowlistedCommand never consults it.

adversarial.desc: The new case does NOT pass options.timeoutMs (or timeoutMs in any options object) to runSingleAllowlistedCommand. If it did, the configured-override bug would be bypassed and the test would be meaninglessly green on main — a false-green RED test.

The new case calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand specifically — NOT runValidationCommand or executeValidationPlan (those paths already honor timeoutMs and are covered by sections 3-5). The test must exercise the exact function the evidence tools use.

Section 6b's current PASS is attributable specifically to the timedOut===true/code===124 assertions succeeding (not merely not-throwing) - confirmed by reading the assertion source directly, and by the red_evidence.json record showing the pre-fix failure was exactly this same assertion (not a config parse failure, allowlist rejection, import error, or missing temp file).

The command string passed to runSingleAllowlistedCommand uses a bare allowlisted executable (e.g. node) as its first token so it passes parseAllowlistedCommand allowlist check — the test must not fail at the allowlist gate.
No new entry is added to the project-root lattice.config.json (the smoke is already registered there per its docstring); the temp config is written only to the ephemeral tmpdir projectRoot.

items.title: Thread validate.commands[].timeoutMs into runSingleAllowlistedCommand via configuredValidationCommands
items.context: In runSingleAllowlistedCommand (validation-executor.ts:584-596) or its callers in checklist.ts, match the pinned command's parsed {executable,args} against configuredValidationCommands(projectRoot) (handlers/verifier.ts:224) entries by exact {command,args} equality, and pass the matched entry's .timeoutMs into options.timeoutMs before constructing the ValidationCommand, falling back to DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS when no entry matches or the caller already supplied an explicit options.timeoutMs. Do not modify resolveCommandTimeoutMs or the lattice validate path (executeValidationPlan/runValidationCommand), which already work correctly.
items.userSees: verification_evidence_add / _batch_add / verification_run against a pinned command with a configured timeoutMs override now respect that budget instead of always capping at 270s; commands with no configured override keep today's 270s default unchanged; the CHK-001 smoke passes.
excludes: packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts is read-only for this story: runSingleAllowlistedCommand already accepts options.timeoutMs, and resolveCommandTimeoutMs/executeValidationPlan/runValidationCommand are explicitly out of scope per scope-boundary.json - no modification, only imported (parseAllowlistedCommand) and invoked (runSingleAllowlistedCommand) as-is.
packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts is read-only for this story: configuredValidationCommands is reused exactly as-is via a new import from checklist.ts; no modification to verifier.ts.

happy.desc: Configured timeoutMs flows to runSingleAllowlistedCommand: build succeeds (npm --prefix packages/main run build) and CHK-001 RED case now passes (node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js exits 0). The 700ms-configured command that sleeps ~1.5s yields timedOut===true and code===124, proving the config override was threaded through all the way to the spawn.

All 4 call sites route through the single shared resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs helper. Diff of checklist.ts shows exactly 4 call sites (~lines 1557, 1648, 1779, 1858) changed from (command, cwd) => runSingleAllowlistedCommand(command, root, { cwd }) to include timeoutMs: resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs(root, command). No duplicated matching logic exists outside the one helper.

validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts are byte-for-byte unmodified: git diff HEAD -- packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts produces empty output. resolveCommandTimeoutMs, runValidationCommand, executeValidationPlan, and configuredValidationCommands are all reused read-only.

Unmatched commands preserve the 270s default. resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns match?.timeoutMs. When no configuredValidationCommands entry matches by exact {command,args}, match is undefined so the return is undefined. This feeds into runSingleAllowlistedCommand options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS (270_000ms) at line 595, preserving today s behavior for unconfigured commands.

edge.desc: Bare-string config entries (no args/timeoutMs object) do not inject a spurious timeout. configuredValidationCommands handles bare strings via commandFromString which never sets timeoutMs. resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs finds a match but match.timeoutMs is undefined, so it returns undefined and runSingleAllowlistedCommand falls back to DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS. No behavioral change for bare-string configured commands.

Parsing parity between tokenizeCommandString (used by parseAllowlistedCommand on the pinned command) and splitShellWords (used by commandFromString on bare-string config entries). For allowlist-legal commands (no shell metacharacters — blocked by VERIFICATION_COMMAND_EXECUTABLE_ALLOWLIST and SHELL_META_RE), both tokenizers produce identical {executable, args}. Verify no divergence for quoting or whitespace in allowlist-legal commands.

Shell-style config entries (shell:true) cannot false-positive-match pinned commands. configuredValidationCommands sets shell:true and stores the entire raw string in .command with empty .args for entries containing shell metacharacters. parseAllowlistedCommand rejects shell metacharacters via the allowlist. Therefore no pinned command can ever have an executable matching a shell-style entry. The strict {command,args} match correctly returns undefined.

Config entry with timeoutMs:0 or negative value. configuredValidationCommands passes through typeof entry.timeoutMs === number entries verbatim. resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns that value. runSingleAllowlistedCommand sets options.timeoutMs to 0 (not nullish). But resolveCommandTimeoutMs (line 76) rejects non-positive values and falls back to DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS. The existing safety net handles this — no new vulnerability introduced.

Import does not create a circular dependency. tsc build succeeds (npm --prefix packages/main run build). Import graph is one-way: checklist.ts imports from verifier.ts (new edge for configuredValidationCommands) and from validation-executor.ts (existing edge, now also parseAllowlistedCommand). Neither verifier.ts nor validation-executor.ts imports from checklist.ts.

adversarial.desc: Attacker crafts a pinned command with extra whitespace or quoting to evade timeout matching. parseAllowlistedCommand normalizes via tokenizeCommandString (strips quotes, collapses whitespace). configuredValidationCommands normalizes via splitShellWords (identical behavior for allowlist-legal inputs). Both produce the same canonical {executable, args} for equivalent commands. Extra whitespace or redundant quoting is stripped during tokenization — an attacker cannot use formatting tricks to dodge a configured timeout because matching operates on parsed tokens, not raw strings.

Attacker pins a command sharing only the executable (same node binary, different args) to steal a high-timeout config entry budget. resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs matches by strict equality on BOTH c.command === executable AND full args array (length + element-wise ===). A command sharing only the executable but differing in any single arg returns no match, falling back to the 270s default. CHK-003 adds explicit regression coverage for this disambiguation case.

Attacker modifies lattice.config.json to inject a very large timeoutMs hoping to hang evidence collection indefinitely. Not a new attack surface — lattice.config.json is already trusted project configuration (same trust boundary as validate.commands used by lattice validate). resolveCommandTimeoutMs already clamps to MAX_NODE_TIMER_DELAY_MS. The fix reuses the identical code path (runValidationCommand -> resolveCommandTimeoutMs) that already enforces this ceiling. No new unbounded timeout vector.

TOCTOU architectural claim confirmed by direct source reading (not by a dynamic race-simulation test, since a single deterministic run cannot demonstrate a race's absence): resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs and runSingleAllowlistedCommand's call sites in checklist.ts read config synchronously via loadConfig then capture the resolved value in a local variable before the async spawn - byte-for-byte the same pattern as the pre-existing lattice-validate path (runValidationCommand -> resolveCommandTimeoutMs), independently confirmed by two REVIEW-phase reviewers reading the actual source.

items.title: Regression coverage: unmatched commands keep the 270s default, and matching does not cross-match by executable alone
items.context: Add coverage that (a) a pinned command with NO matching entry in validate.commands[] still gets the 270s default (no behavior change for the common case), and (b) two distinct configured commands that share an executable but differ in args do not cross-match each other's timeoutMs (matching must compare the full parsed args array, not just the executable).
items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js` prints `validate-command-timeout smoke passed: N assertions` with N increased by the new unmatched-default and args-disambiguation checks, and exits 0 - no FAIL lines for either new case.

happy.desc: Write a temp lattice.config.json to a fresh tmpdir projectRoot with two validate.commands[] entries sharing the same executable (node) but with different args arrays and different timeoutMs values (e.g. 700 and 5000). For each entry, call resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs(root, pinnedCommandString) where pinnedCommandString parses to the exact same {executable, args} as that config entry. Assert each call returns that entry's own exact timeoutMs value, not the other's. WHY: proves the matching logic compares the full {command, args} tuple and returns the correct per-entry budget.

The full smoke suite (sections 1-5 from prior CHK items plus CHK-001's section 6) still passes after adding the new CHK-003 assertions — the total assertion count logged on the final 'passed: N assertions' line increases but no pre-existing assertion regresses. WHY: ensures CHK-003's additions are purely additive and do not break earlier coverage.

All new assertions are pure synchronous calls to resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs against a temp lattice.config.json — no real timed subprocess waits — so the test completes in sub-second time regardless of the timeoutMs values declared in config. WHY: CHK-003's intent is unit-level coverage of the matching logic; adding wall-clock waits would make the smoke slow and fragile.

edge.desc: Unmatched-default: the temp config has one or more configured validate.commands[] entries, but the pinned command string parses to an {executable, args} pair that matches NONE of them (different args or entirely different executable). Assert resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns undefined — not zero, not the first entry's timeoutMs, not DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS. The undefined return is the signal for the caller to fall through to the 270s default via the existing options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_VALIDATE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS path. WHY: the common case (a pinned command with no config override) must remain unchanged.

Args-length mismatch: config entry has args [a, b] with timeoutMs X; pinned command has the same executable but only args [a] (a strict prefix of the config entry's args). Assert resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns undefined. WHY: must not partial-match on a prefix of the args array — the args.length guard fires before element comparison.

Args-content mismatch: config entry has args [-e, foo] with timeoutMs X; pinned command has the same executable and same args length but different content ([-e, bar]). Assert resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns undefined. WHY: element-wise string equality is required, not just length equality; proves the every() comparator fires.

adversarial.desc: Cross-match by executable alone: temp config has TWO entries with the same executable (node) but distinct args arrays and distinct timeoutMs values. For each of the two corresponding pinned command strings, assert resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs returns that specific entry's own timeoutMs — never the other entry's value. A naive implementation that matches by executable alone (or returns the first match regardless of args) would return the wrong budget for one of the two commands. WHY: this is the exact cross-match-by-executable-alone defect the plan's title warns about.

No silent wrong match: when the pinned command's executable matches a config entry's command field but the args differ, the helper must return undefined rather than returning the wrong entry's timeoutMs. Assert that for a pinned command whose executable exists in config but whose args match no entry, the return value is strictly undefined (=== undefined). This distinguishes a clean 'no match' (caller safely falls through to 270s) from a silent 'wrong match' (caller unknowingly applies another command's budget — a latent timeout bug that could either truncate a legitimate long-running receipt or over-extend a budget for a command that should be killed sooner). WHY: undefined is the only safe sentinel; any numeric return from an unmatched lookup is a potential misattribution.

items.title: Acceptance verification: the timeoutMs-config-override fix builds and its full regression suite passes
items.context: Provides a stable, freshly-pinnable verification intent for the ProofStory acceptance binding (AB-001), distinct from CHK-001/002/003 whose individual verificationEvidence pins are permanently locked to a since-superseded selector (assertion count) from a premature early batch submission. No new code: this item just records real, current mechanical evidence that packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js (already built by CHK-001/002/003) builds and passes, using a stable substring selector that does not embed the assertion count so it will not go stale as coverage grows.
items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js` prints a line starting with `validate-command-timeout smoke passed:` and exits 0.

happy.desc: node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js exits 0 and prints output starting with the stable prefix validate-command-timeout smoke passed: (not asserting the exact count, which grows as coverage is added).

verificationEvidence.note: Stable substring selector (no assertion count embedded) so this pin never goes stale as coverage grows. Tool-executed: the smoke genuinely builds and passes (currently 45 assertions across sections 1-16, covering the timeoutMs-config-override fix end to end).

auditLog.reason: Fixing a discovered gap: the ProofStory acceptance binding requires at least one verificationIntentRef with genuine non-waiver passing evidence, but every existing CHK-001/002/003 intentRef is permanently pin-locked to a stale count-embedding selector. This new item provides a clean, stably-selectable target.
